turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mrs. Iyer, come this side. I will check the BP and pulse before the doctor calls you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Sister, this itching is too much, I cannot even sit properly. Is my pressure shooting up because of the rash? I am really worried.

[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): One thirty over... no, one twenty-eight over eighty-two. Pulse eighty-eight, temperature thirty-six point eight, oxygen ninety-eight percent. It is all fine, you can go in.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sit. What is the problem today?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, I am having a very itchy rash on both arms and the stomach. I am so scared, will it spread to my face also?
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): When did it start?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Sunday we were at my cousin's house and I ate prawns, then I started that new cream, and the antibiotic from the dentist also, and I thought maybe—
[SEG0008] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, she is not answering you. The rash actually—
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): —at night I am not sleeping at all, I keep scratching, even my husband woke up. Sorry, I am very tense only.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): How many days has the rash been there?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Two days... no, three days. From Monday morning itself.
[SEG0012] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I saw it already on Saturday when I was helping her dress. So it is five days, not three.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): All right, call it about three to five days. Where is the rash now?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Both arms, the stomach, and a little on the neck. Is the neck dangerous, doctor, so close to the throat?
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Those prawns were not fresh, I told my cousin only, and the cream is a white tube with a pink cap, I put it for dryness—
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever. Yes or no?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any swelling of the lips, or trouble breathing?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Will you admit me? Please, I have office tomorrow, I cannot stay in hospital, I am very scared of that.
[SEG0021] person_4 (CAREGIVER): In the auto she was breathing normally, and the lips were normal also. I was watching her only.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am asking her. Any breathing trouble?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no breathing problem, and the lips are normal. But am I getting admitted or not?
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): No admission. Any vomiting?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No vomiting.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is there pain, or only the itch?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): It is itching like anything, and a little burning on the rash. I had body ache so I took Crocin.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is the body ache still there?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Only a little now. The itch is the main thing, it is worse at night.
[SEG0030] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She was scratching till about two o'clock. I had to hold her hands.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Which antibiotic are you on, and what dose?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): The dentist gave amoxicillin, two-fifty... no, not that. It is Azee, azithromycin, five hundred milligrams, once a day, since four days, for the tooth.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): By mouth?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, the tablet, after food. Should I stop it? If the tooth swells up I don't know what I will do.
[SEG0035] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She took today's morning dose, I gave it myself. It is once a day only.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): What is the name of the new cream?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know the proper name. It is the white tube only, pink cap, the chemist said for dry skin. I started it one week... no, four days back, twice a day, on the legs.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): So you cannot name it.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Kindly tell me which one did this, the prawns or the cream or the Azee? I have to know, otherwise I cannot relax.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any known allergy to medicines?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing. No allergy to any tablet or food, I am very sure.
[SEG0042] person_4 (CAREGIVER): That is not what her mother told me. In childhood penicillin gave her the same itchy red rash, and they stopped it. It is written in the old diary at home.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): That is not true, I deny it. I have taken penicillin so many times, no rash, nothing. Why are you bringing this up now?
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): So one of you says a penicillin rash in childhood, and you say no. I cannot settle that here.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Please do not write penicillin allergy on my file. Will other doctors refuse me antibiotics forever? I am really frightened.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me see. There is a red rash on both forearms and the abdomen, no blisters, and a few spots on the neck. Lips are not swollen. Chest is clear.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it gone into the blood? Do I need a blood test today? Someone told me about a patch test, will that hurt, will it leave a scar?
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): No blood test today. This may be an allergic rash from the prawns, the cream, or the azithromycin, and I cannot say which. That is a working impression only.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Then what all should I stop? Can I eat curd and rice tonight? I have hardly eaten.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stop the azithromycin. Stop that white cream. Avoid prawns for now. Curd and rice are fine.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): And for the itch? Will the tablet make me sleepy? I have to go to office.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will give cetirizine ten milligrams, one tablet at night, for five days. It can make you sleepy, so not in the daytime.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): My neighbour takes twenty milligrams. Is ten too small for me? What if the itch comes in the afternoon?
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ten milligrams is the dose. Do not take twenty. Start with the night dose.
[SEG0055] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I will give it at night. Should I bring that white tube next time, so you can read the name?
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, bring the tube. If the rash has not settled in one week, we might arrange a patch test. Not today.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): If my tongue swells in the night, what do I do, come running? And the patch test will not scar, no? I keep thinking of the worst.
[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the tongue swells or you cannot breathe, go to emergency straight away. A patch test does not leave a scar. We are not booking it now.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): The dentist said I must finish the Azee. If I stop, the tooth pain will come back. How many days are left on it?
[SEG0060] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Two days were left... or is it three? I am not sure, the strip is at home.
[SEG0061] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stop it anyway. If the tooth pain returns, see the dentist. Do not restart the Azee on your own.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): And the follow up? If it becomes worse on day two itself, do I still wait the whole week? I will not stop worrying.
[SEG0063] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back after one week for review. If it is spreading fast or you get breathing trouble, come earlier, do not wait.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): Will the marks stay on the skin? There is a function next month. My mother says coconut oil cools it, can I apply a little?
[SEG0065] person_3 (DOCTOR): No coconut oil. No new creams. The marks usually fade, and I will not promise a date.
[SEG0066] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She will ask ten more people after this. Doctor, the Crocin, should that stop also?
[SEG0067] person_3 (DOCTOR): Crocin only if the body ache needs it. Not for the rash.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): I took one five-hundred Crocin yesterday and one this morning. Is that too much for me? My head is a little heavy also.
[SEG0069] person_3 (DOCTOR): Five hundred is a normal dose. The headache is mild, and I am not chasing it today. Take the cetirizine at night, stop the Azee and the cream, and review in one week.
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): If the itch is still there tomorrow morning, can I call the clinic, or do I just wait? I will not sleep, thinking about it.
[SEG0071] person_1 (NURSE): Reception will give you the cetirizine slip outside. Call if it is an emergency, otherwise it is the one week review the doctor said.
